title: Jack Mildren: Wishbone QB Turned Oklahoma Lieutenant Governor
question: Which OU quarterback became lieutenant governor of Oklahoma?
answer: Jack Mildren, OU's quarterback from 1969 to 1971, was elected Oklahoma lieutenant governor in 1990 and served from 1991 to 1995.
summary: Jack Mildren quarterbacked OU from 1969 to 1971, ran its record-setting wishbone, then became lieutenant governor, a banker and a sports radio host.
body: Jack Mildren came to Norman from Abilene, Texas, and played quarterback for Oklahoma from 1969 through 1971. He is remembered as the first quarterback to run OU's wishbone, the offense Chuck Fairbanks' staff installed in 1970, and he made it hum.

His 1971 team went 11-1 and averaged 472.4 rushing yards per game, an NCAA record. Mildren accounted for four touchdowns in the famous 35-31 Game of the Century loss at Nebraska, then was named Sugar Bowl MVP after a 40-22 win over Auburn. He earned second-team All-America and Academic All-America honors that year.
The Baltimore Colts drafted him in the second round in 1972, and he spent three seasons in the NFL as a defensive back with the Colts and the New England Patriots before returning home.

Mildren's second act was in business and public life. He owned an oil company and later became vice chairman of Arvest Bank Group. A Democrat, he was elected lieutenant governor in 1990 and served from 1991 to 1995. In 1994 he ran for governor and finished second to Frank Keating in a three-way race.

He never drifted far from football, either. In later years Mildren hosted a daily sports radio show on WKY in Oklahoma City. He died of stomach cancer in May 2008 at age 58. Few Sooners have been as comfortable under center, in a boardroom and at the State Capitol.
